title: Which of each pair is greater?
description: Three pairs of small lengths are changed to thousandths and compared by their counts. The counts are checked again in a different place.
teaching_notes: One idea: change both lengths in a pair to thousandths, and the larger count is the greater length. Watch for children who compare only the top numbers.

source: Figure it Out (end of chapter), Q13
video_script.why: The child knows how many thousandths fill each bigger place and now compares pairs by that.
video_script.substitution: Change both lengths in a pair to thousandths, and the larger count is the greater length.
video_script.anchor: three pairs of small lengths, each pair needing its greater one
video_script.payoff_line: Change both to thousandths, then compare the counts

final_answer.value: (a) 1/10 is greater (b) 90 thousandths is greater (c) 90 hundredths is greater
final_answer.spoken: one tenth, ninety thousandths and ninety hundredths

video_script.fraction_reading: tenth, hundredth and thousandth are said as words
hold_back: (a) 1/10 is greater (b) 90 thousandths is greater (c) 90 hundredths is greater
maths_rules: (b) one hundredth = 10 thousandths; 90 > 10, so 90 thousandths is greater
(c) 90 hundredths = 90 x 10 = 900 thousandths; 900 > 1, so 90 hundredths is greater
check: in hundredths, 10/1000 = 1 hundredth and 1/10 = 10 hundredths; 10 > 1
the slip: 10 is more than 1 on top, but the bottom numbers differ
video_script.design: The three pairs stay in the anchor band all video; each pair is changed to thousandths in the working band, one step per pair, then checked in hundredths.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; three pairs: (a) 10/1000 or 1/10, (b) one hundredth or 90 thousandths, (c) one thousandth or 90 hundredths; a question mark in the anchor band
narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>Three pairs of very small lengths are given, written in different places.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which one of each pair is greater?

beats.on_screen: the pairs stay on the board; Keeko sits beside them as the child
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a unit bar with a tenth, a hundredth and a thousandth marked; a tenth = 100 thousandths, a hundredth = 10 thousandths

marks.bar: a unit bar is drawn with a tenth, a hundredth and a thousandth marked
marks.count: the thousandths in a tenth and in a hundredth are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='bar'/>Remember the unit bar and its small parts, where the thousandth is the smallest of them all.
<bookmark mark='count'/>A tenth holds one hundred thousandths, and a hundredth holds ten thousandths.

beats.on_screen: Given: (a) 10/1000 or 1/10  (b) one hundredth or 90 thousandths  (c) one thousandth or 90 hundredths
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the three pairs from the question.

beats.on_screen: To find: the greater one in each pair
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the greater one in each pair, by changing both to thousandths and comparing.

beats.on_screen: Step 1 (a): 10/1000 = 10 thousandths; 1/10 = 100 thousandths; 100 is more than 10
narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, pair a, where ten over one thousand is ten thousandths.
<bookmark mark='tenth'/>One tenth is the same as one hundred thousandths.
<bookmark mark='cmp'/>One hundred is more than ten, so one tenth is the greater one.

beats.on_screen: Step 2 (b): one hundredth = 10 thousandths; 90 thousandths; 90 is more than 10

marks.hundredth: one hundredth is changed to 10 thousandths

narration: <bookmark mark='hundredth'/>Step two, pair b, where one hundredth is the same as ten thousandths.
<bookmark mark='cmp'/>Ninety thousandths is more than ten thousandths, so ninety thousandths is the greater one.

beats.on_screen: Step 3 (c): 90 hundredths = 90 x 10 = 900 thousandths; one thousandth is 1; 900 is more than 1

marks.change: 90 hundredths is changed to 90 x 10 thousandths

narration: <bookmark mark='change'/>Step three, pair c, where each hundredth is ten thousandths, so ninety hundredths is ninety times ten.
<bookmark mark='cmp'/>That is nine hundred thousandths, far more than one thousandth, and ninety hundredths is the greater one.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check pair a in hundredths: 10/1000 = 1 hundredth; 1/10 = 10 hundredths; 10 is more than 1

marks.check: pair a is changed to hundredths

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, put the answer back by checking pair a in hundredths.
Ten over one thousand is one hundredth, and one tenth is ten hundredths.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Ten is more than one again, so one tenth is greater.

beats.on_screen: Answer: (a) 1/10 is greater (b) 90 thousandths is greater (c) 90 hundredths is greater
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Change both to thousandths, then compare the counts.
One tenth, ninety thousandths and ninety hundredths are the greater ones.
